SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire

Rocket company and AI model builder to combine as billionaire envisions data centres in space
  • SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire on x (opens in a new window)
  • SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire on facebook (opens in a new window)
  • SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire on linkedin (opens in a new window)
  • SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire on whatsapp (opens in a new window)
  • SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire on x (opens in a new window)
  • SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire on facebook (opens in a new window)
  • SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire on linkedin (opens in a new window)
  • SpaceX buys xAI uniting crucial parts of Elon Musk’s empire on whatsapp (opens in a new window)

George Hammond and Hannah Murphy in San Francisco

PublishedFebruary 2 2026

Jump to comments section
Unlock the Editor’s Digest for free

Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter.

Elon Musk’s SpaceX has acquired his AI group xAI, the billionaire said on Monday, furthering his ambition to develop powerful tools powered by data centres in space.

Musk did not disclose financial terms of the deal, but the two companies together are worth just over $1tn following recent funding rounds.

The merger was part of Musk’s plan to develop “a sentient sun to understand the Universe and extend the light of consciousness to the stars!” he wrote in Monday’s announcement.

Bret Johnsen, SpaceX’s chief financial officer, was scheduled to hold a call with investors in the company on Monday afternoon to discuss the buyout, according to two people familiar with the matter.

SpaceX was recently valued at $800bn in a secondary stock sale, while xAI was valued at $230bn in a recent funding round.

The news comes after xAI merged with Musk’s social media platform X in March last year. The takeover valued the overall group at $113bn, pricing xAI at $80bn with X at $33bn. Musk bought X, formerly known as Twitter, for $44bn in October 2022.

xAI has been rapidly fundraising as it races to build out the AI infrastructure needed to train and power its models and gain an edge over competitors such as OpenAI, Meta and Google. 

This is a developing story. Additional reporting by Stephen Morris in San Francisco and Ivan Levingston in London
